question: Should OpenClaw adopt the RFC's one-Claw-one-new-agent core lifecycle and authorize this managed-workspace-file slice to proceed in the stacked landing order?
rationale: The patch introduces a new persistent core lifecycle and trust boundary; code correctness cannot decide whether that product and compatibility contract should become supported OpenClaw behavior.

options.title: Accept and land in order
options.body: Accept or explicitly sponsor the RFC, then review and merge the prerequisite stack before this slice.

options.title: Narrow before acceptance
options.body: Approve only the agent, workspace, and file lifecycle while deferring broader package, MCP, cron, update, or export contracts.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Keep the stack open without landing until the RFC and upgrade/recovery model receive further maintainer review.

recommendation.title: Accept and land in order
recommendation.body: Accept or explicitly sponsor the RFC, then review and merge the prerequisite stack before this slice.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the concrete product-model and schema revision adopted by the RFC and this implementation slice.
